flavor.component_cooler.t1.broken: The fins have been crushed together. Where air once passed, there is only metal.
flavor.component_cooler.t1.intact: Its first installer studied the mounting clips for half an hour. The instructions were right by their feet.
flavor.component_cooler.t2.broken: The mounting bracket bends sideways. The two towers no longer line up, like neighbors after an argument.
flavor.component_cooler.t2.intact: Two towers side by side. The builder measures first to see whether the case panel will still close.
flavor.component_cooler.t3.broken: A heat pipe has kinked sharply. All that weight failed to protect the most delicate part.
flavor.component_cooler.t3.intact: Lift it and you understand why a cooler might need a little support of its own.
flavor.component_cooler.t4.broken: A hose fitting has split. A dried trail of coolant runs down to the radiator's lower edge.
flavor.component_cooler.t4.intact: From a copper base to a full radiator. The builder now has to find seating for the hoses.
flavor.component_cooler.t5.broken: A diagonal crack crosses the screen and the pump housing is chipped. The polished face has finally come apart.
flavor.component_cooler.t5.intact: Even the cooler has a little screen. There is more to look at inside the case than on the desk.
flavor.component_cpu.t1.broken: A corner has chipped off the substrate. The lettering on the lid is in much better shape.
flavor.component_cpu.t1.intact: Once kept office hours alongside its user. Its most frequent instruction was probably 'save'.
flavor.component_cpu.t2.broken: A deep gouge cuts across the underside, interrupting a path through the dense contacts.
flavor.component_cpu.t2.intact: Never in the most expensive column, but remembered from plenty of first builds.
flavor.component_cpu.t3.broken: Heat has browned the edge of the lid. The seller's claim of heavy workloads suddenly carries some weight.
flavor.component_cpu.t3.intact: Bought for work, supposedly. The first thing launched after assembly was a game.
flavor.component_cpu.t4.broken: The substrate crack runs beneath the lid. A fingertip-sized fracture has swallowed a considerable budget.
flavor.component_cpu.t4.intact: On its first boot, the owner watched the temperature so long that the original plan slipped away.
flavor.component_cpu.t5.broken: The lid has shifted, exposing a gap. Advanced fabrication is still vulnerable to an ordinary hard knock.
flavor.component_cpu.t5.intact: The model name keeps getting longer. The chip stays small; the bill does not.
flavor.component_fan.t1.broken: Half a blade is missing. The others still look dutifully ready for work.
flavor.component_fan.t1.intact: When it spins up on the test bench, the paper scraps notice it starting work before the shopkeeper does.
flavor.component_fan.t2.broken: The frame has split around a screw hole. Tightening things harder is clearly not always the answer.
flavor.component_fan.t2.intact: One screw was missing from the bag. The shopkeeper supplied another in a different color.
flavor.component_fan.t3.broken: The hub sits crooked. Blades have scraped a half-circle into the frame. The silence came afterward.
flavor.component_fan.t3.intact: You have to lean close to hear it running. The old hard drive beside it suddenly seems very talkative.
flavor.component_fan.t4.broken: The broken blade ends in a ragged stump. The familiar color scheme makes the damage hard to miss.
flavor.component_fan.t4.intact: Someone always dislikes this color scheme. Someone else comes looking specifically for it.
flavor.component_fan.t5.broken: The light ring is cracked and the blades jammed. Its last appearance probably was not on a display stand.
flavor.component_fan.t5.intact: One costs as much as several ordinary fans. The customer still wants a whole case full.
flavor.component_gpu.t1.broken: A broken fan blade lies inside the shroud. Years of matches ended with a single drop.
flavor.component_gpu.t1.intact: An old companion for old games. Lower the settings a little and everyone gets along.
flavor.component_gpu.t2.broken: The bracket is twisted and the board edge cracked. The seller insists it was just a bump in transit.
flavor.component_gpu.t2.intact: The buyer examines it three times, then asks how much will be left for food this month.
flavor.component_gpu.t3.broken: A piece of the shroud is missing. The exposed board carries a troubling patch of brown scorch.
flavor.component_gpu.t3.intact: Still rendering in the background, already gaming in the foreground. Its last owner knew how to spend a wait.
flavor.component_gpu.t4.broken: The heavy heatsink has warped the board. All that performance did nothing to soften the landing.
flavor.component_gpu.t4.intact: The long card reaches past the motherboard. The cables need to relocate before it can move in.
flavor.component_gpu.t5.broken: Charred black covers the components. The model is recognizable; nobody wants to name a price first.
flavor.component_gpu.t5.intact: Whenever it is on the counter, every ring of the doorbell makes the shopkeeper look up to see who is coming.
flavor.component_hdd.t1.broken: A dent sits right over the platter. The small rattle inside is not a sound you want to hear twice.
flavor.component_hdd.t1.intact: Nothing vast. Enough for years of documents and a few old games you cannot bring yourself to delete.
flavor.component_hdd.t2.broken: A corner of the connector is missing. A few millimeters of broken contact now separate you from the data.
flavor.component_hdd.t2.intact: Every file named 'final version' somehow has room for one more revision here.
flavor.component_hdd.t3.broken: A black burn marks the underside board. The fate of dozens of folders is suddenly uncertain.
flavor.component_hdd.t3.intact: Room for people who keep every file. Sorting them is a job for another day.
flavor.component_hdd.t4.broken: A deep gouge cuts into the edge. Somewhere, an all-night server room is down one shift worker.
flavor.component_hdd.t4.intact: Pulled from a rack whose lights never went out. Retirement looks more like a shift change.
flavor.component_hdd.t5.broken: The split seal tells its own story. Nobody will vouch for whatever once lived inside.
flavor.component_hdd.t5.intact: Print out everything it could hold and the shop's shelving would have to move out first.
flavor.component_motherboard.t1.broken: A corner has snapped off. Exposed copper traces end abruptly, like roads leading nowhere.
flavor.component_motherboard.t1.intact: Pulled from a little office PC. It still seems to carry the drowsiness of a Monday morning.
flavor.component_motherboard.t2.broken: A shard of plastic sits in a cracked slot. Whoever pulled the part out missed the release latch.
flavor.component_motherboard.t2.intact: The box is gone, but the build list survives. Its line is the only one that was never crossed out.
flavor.component_motherboard.t3.broken: The power section is scorched brown. Beneath the heatsink lies an accident omitted from the invoice.
flavor.component_motherboard.t3.intact: The traces wind neatly around every screw hole. Better organized than the ledger behind the counter.
flavor.component_motherboard.t4.broken: A crack runs beneath the armor. All that imposing metal cannot conceal the severed traces.
flavor.component_motherboard.t4.intact: The heatsink armor dominates the board. You have to lean closer to find the model name.
flavor.component_motherboard.t5.broken: Several rows of socket contacts lean sideways. Even the damage is too precise to see at a glance.
flavor.component_motherboard.t5.intact: After hearing the price, the customer asks again: is that for the board or the whole computer?
flavor.component_psu.t1.broken: A black scorch ring surrounds the cable exit. The smell of burnt plastic still lingers.
flavor.component_psu.t1.intact: The least remarkable metal box in the case decides when every other part wakes up.
flavor.component_psu.t2.broken: The cable bundle is neatly tied. The plugs at the far end have melted together.
flavor.component_psu.t2.intact: The '0' and '1' on the switch once puzzled a beginner enough to bring the builder back.
flavor.component_psu.t3.broken: The casing has a deep dent. Something small rolls around inside whenever it moves.
flavor.component_psu.t3.intact: Whoever removed it coiled each cable separately. For once, no untangling is required.
flavor.component_psu.t4.broken: A scorch mark runs across the intake. Expensive cables did nothing to prevent whatever happened.
flavor.component_psu.t4.intact: A dot of red paint marks one connector: a reminder not to put that cable in the wrong place again.
flavor.component_psu.t5.broken: The nameplate still shines like a mirror. The seller put the burnt side face down.
flavor.component_psu.t5.intact: A discreet model name, in packaging that treats it like classified equipment.
flavor.component_ram.t1.broken: One contact has chipped away, leaving a gap in an otherwise orderly row of gold.
flavor.component_ram.t1.intact: Remembers everything the programs need all day. Forgets it all the moment the power goes off.
flavor.component_ram.t2.broken: The board has acquired an unwanted curve. A low price will not make the slot any more forgiving.
flavor.component_ram.t2.intact: The seller says you will feel better with another stick. He tells every customer that.
flavor.component_ram.t3.broken: One chip has cracked open. The exposed fracture lies beyond the heat spreader's protection.
flavor.component_ram.t3.intact: Several large programs can finally share the room without asking someone else to leave.
flavor.component_ram.t4.broken: One end of the spreader has peeled away, exposing missing components. The bundle's value came apart with it.
flavor.component_ram.t4.intact: Once one of a pair, now on its own. Its partner is probably busy in another computer.
flavor.component_ram.t5.broken: A scorch crosses several chips. The handsome casing now serves only to earn a second glance.
flavor.component_ram.t5.intact: The capacity is printed large, the price small. A familiar trick on this counter.
flavor.computer_case.t1.broken: One corner took a hard hit. The panel is keeping its secrets better than the seller did.
flavor.computer_case.t1.intact: The thin panels let the fans do the talking. Still, every first build needs a home.
flavor.computer_case.t2.broken: The panel has buckled and cables poke through the gap. Moving day clearly went badly.
flavor.computer_case.t2.intact: The cables tuck away behind the tray. One less tangled mess under the desk.
flavor.computer_case.t3.broken: The front frame is bent and the feet no longer line up. It insists on the counter's flattest spot.
flavor.computer_case.t3.intact: Black panels, straight lines, no fuss. It looks reassuring next to the rest of the stock.
flavor.computer_case.t4.broken: Cracks divide the display panel into fragments. Somehow, the view inside is worse than before.
flavor.computer_case.t4.intact: Behind all that glass, every cable is on display. There is nowhere to hide a sloppy build.
flavor.computer_case.t5.broken: One corner has caved in. The rest still has the imposing bulk of a building awaiting demolition.
flavor.computer_case.t5.intact: It takes up half the counter. The shopkeeper is reconsidering the policy of paying per item.

text.01fc8dc622e5: Displaying this sign raises the PC Materials Seller's daily visit chance from 30% to 75%, and the PC Parts Thief's from 20% to 40%. The seller is eligible from day 5 and the thief from day 12. Multiple signs do not stack. Each visit is rolled separately when the shop opens; successful visitors join the end of the day's queue and are not shown in the vanilla Expected Normal Customers list. Displaying intact T4 or T5 parts can still attract the PC Buyer.
text.055f6bdf0038: Here are the parts and materials. See anything you need?
text.150a32bc88cf: All memory sticks must be the same tier
text.2fe62616a758: Once it lights up, people carrying bags of spare parts know which door to try.
text.34ccec0329de: Obtain Vesper's 0504 business card once to unlock calls to her permanently.
text.39c95467b293: You must own the teardown screwdriver to use it.
text.3ed437206a5f: Part tiers are more than three steps apart
text.3f2ae7609f09: Got decent parts or a tidy value build? I'll take a look.
text.47b2c0f573a3: Found a few working PC parts. Brought screws and electronic parts too; they're always handy for repairs.
text.4887c4447d04: I buy working PC parts and qualifying complete builds up to T3.
text.4c405ee461f5: Unlock failed. Check the game log.
text.5eb52273543e: This case is jammed. Use the teardown screwdriver to open it.
text.69e3a29d2368: Remove the part from the PC case before repairing it.
text.6a7bc1081071: I can't afford parts this good.
text.723b3b1739c9: Found these on my rounds. See anything you like? I stop by every Friday if you want to trade.
text.72e9b91a379f: You can only unlock a PC case you own.
text.79392d2f43d1: I buy working PC parts and complete builds up to T3. No bottleneck builds or half-empty cases.
text.8bf853ae1d76: Sure, I'll bring a few rigs over. See you at the shop.
text.8d59d9e16dff: I've got a spare tower gathering dust. Make me an offer.
text.996b4925c50c: Build data could not be synchronized. Close and reopen the case, then test again.
text.a3ec80c70209: I've got cash to spend and a few towers to sell. Anything catch your eye? You can disassemble and assemble parts in the workroom.
text.ab200af82511: You do not own a locked PC case.
text.b18ca73d66e9: Unlocked. Double-click the case to retrieve its parts.
text.b7bb85ea4318: You can only use this while at the shop.
text.bb9a3627859b: That'll do. Let's agree on a price.
text.c9eaa60d077e: I only buy working T3+ PC parts. Complete builds must have every required part, and every installed part must be working and at least T3.
text.da4324746524: Show me the good stuff. I don't deal in anything below T3.
text.e53d5207f70f: This PC case is not locked.
text.e8ccfb408f51:
Vesper's number: 0504. Buying or actually owning this card once permanently unlocks calls and shopping with her, even if you lose it. A shop visit or card offer alone does not unlock the contact. Phone visits have a three-day cooldown. The lower-district builder who sells this card stops by every Friday.
Mod QQ group: 157249439
